nodes.name: Carbon-confined RuCr nanoparticle synthesis
nodes.procedure: The mixture of metal precursors (Ruthenium acetylacetonate and Chromium acetylacetonate) and potassium bromide (KBr) was annealed under reduction atmosphere (5% H₂/95% N₂) under 300°C for 90 min. During the calcination process, the metal precursors were melted into liquid and decomposed on the surface of KBr which functioned as hard template to suppress aggregation via modifying the diffusion rate of metal atoms under nucleation process. After naturally cooling down to room temperature, the RuCr@C catalyst was obtained after washing the residual with deionized water and ethanol to remove KBr and possible contaminants.

nodes.description: HER performance in N2-saturated 1.0 M KOH (RuCr@C, Ru@C, Pt/C, Ru/C)
nodes.source_text: Figure 2a shows the linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) of those catalysts in N2 saturated 1M KOH solution with a scan rate of 5mVs−1 at room temperature. As expected, the RuCr@C catalyst exhibited the optimal HER activity. An ultralow overpotential of 19mV is required for the RuCr@C catalyst to afford a current density of 10mAcm−2... The largest exchange current density of 2.14mAcm−2 was achieved on the RuCr@C catalyst... H2 Faraday efficiency of near 100% at an overpotential of 50mV. Tafel slope of 23.8... TOF values of RuCr@C at an overpotential of 50mV was 4.25H2s−1... the electrochemical surface area (ECSA) was increased upon Cr incorporation
HER performance of the RuCr@C catalyst was also evaluated in 0.5M H2SO4... the overpotential at 10mA cm−2 in 0.5M H2SO4... are 18
HER performance of the RuCr@C catalyst was also evaluated in... 1.0M phosphate buffered solution (PBS). ...the overpotential at 10mA cm−2 in... 1.0M PBS are 32.6mV

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows ultrafine RuCr@C nanoparticles with uniform size distribution of 2-4 nm encapsulated in carbon substrate (Figure 1b,c).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphologies and microstructures of as crafted RuCr@C catalyst was directly characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Ultrafine nanoparticles with a uniform size distribution ranging from 2 to 4 nm were successfully prepared (Figure 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of RuCr@C show two prominent peaks at 1350 and 1600 cm⁻¹ corresponding to defect-band and graphitic-band, with I_D/I_G ratio of 0.82 indicating abundant defect sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, formation of carbon layers was further characterized by the Raman spectroscopy. Two prominent peaks situated around 1350 and 1600 cm⁻¹ corresponding to defect-band and graphitic-band of carbon materials were observed... The I_D/I_G ratio was determined to be 0.82.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows lattice fringe with spacing of 0.23 nm corresponding to Ru(100) plane in RuCr@C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) scanning TEM (STEM) was employed to determine the atomic structure of the RuCr@C catalyst. As displayed in Figure 1d, a lattice fringe with a spacing of 0.23 nm corresponds to the Ru(100) plane could be clearly identified.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows homogeneous distribution of Ru and Cr throughout RuCr@C catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental distribution of the RuCr@C catalyst was detected by the energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (Figure 1e), the individual elemental map of Ru and Cr indicated their homogeneous distributions throughout the catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines Ru loading of 45.29 wt% in RuCr@C and Ru/Cr atomic ratio of 18.23:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru loading in the RuCr@C catalyst was determined to be 45.29% by the ICP-OES, and the atomic ratio of Ru/Cr was 18.23:1 (Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of RuCr@C shows peaks at 38.4° and 44.0° assigned to Ru(100) and Ru(101) facets, no peaks for chromium species indicating low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of the RuCr@C shown two prominent peaks centered at 38.4° and 44.0° which could be assigned to the (100) and (101) facets of Ru (JCPDS # 65-7646) (Figure 1f), no obvious peak shift was observed relative to Ru@C.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ru 3p peaks at 461.5 eV (3p3/2) and 483.8 eV (3p1/2) confirm metallic Ru in RuCr@C with positive shift vs commercial Ru/C; Cr 2p peaks at 587.2 eV (2p1/2) and 577.0 eV (2p3/2) indicate Cr³⁺ species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution XPS spectra of the Ru 3p regions (Figure 1g) were split into 3p3/2 and 3p1/2 doublets... the Ru 3p peaks located at 461.5 and 483.8 eV could be assigned to metallic Ru 3p3/2 and Ru 3p1/2... The Cr 2p spectra (Figure S5b, Supporting Information) exhibited two broad peaks at 587.2 and 577.0 eV corresponding to Cr2p1/2 and Cr2p3/2, respectively, indicating the presence of high-valence Cr³⁺ species.
